title: Bits & Math

views.title: Bits & Number Theory
views.intro: Know the five bit identities cold (clear lowest set bit, isolate it, read, set, toggle). Number theory in interviews is gcd, fast power, sieve, factorization, modular inverse and nCr mod a prime, plus overflow discipline.
table: popcount via n & (n - 1), counting bits dp
nCr mod prime with factorial tables

files.desc: Single number family, hamming weight, count bits, powers of two/four, reverse bits, missing number, add without +, range AND, subsets by mask, gcd/lcm, powMod, sieve, factorize, nCr, overflow-safe reverse, fraction to decimal

pitfalls: Use `>>>` for logical shifts of negatives and `1L << k` once k reaches 31.
Check overflow BEFORE multiplying or adding (Reverse Integer), or widen to long.
Fermat inverse needs a PRIME modulus; otherwise use extended Euclid.

decisions.a: XOR fold; split by lowest set bit for two uniques
n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit

calibration: SDE2 bar: single number, number of 1 bits, power of two, counting bits, missing number, reverse integer with overflow checks.
SDE3 bar: single number II/III, sum without plus, range AND, bitmask subsets, fast power, sieve, fraction to decimal.
Staff bar (for context): modular arithmetic with inverses and nCr, bit tricks inside dp, and reasoning about overflow and precision systematically.
